Paragraph: You mighty ones, watching the trees on the banks of Pampa, make this river with its propitious waters shine forth. With your golden hue you appear courageous, yet you sigh repeatedly; you wear jute-cloth yet look mighty-shouldered - who are you that distress all the beings of this forest?
Situation/Problem_Faced: Hanuman notices visible signs of sorrow (repeated sighing) beneath the regal, powerful exterior of the princes.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Observes and gently names the visible distress rather than ignoring it, showing empathetic attentiveness.
Outcome/Resolution: Opens space for the strangers' hidden grief to eventually be acknowledged.
Brief_Summary_Spiritual: Hanuman's noticing of Rama's sighs reflects karuna - the capacity to perceive concealed suffering with compassion.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Demonstrates empathetic observation - reading nonverbal cues (sighing) as indicators of underlying emotional distress (grief over Sita's abduction).
